lines.text: Cover a two by six board with dominoes. There are exactly thirteen ways.
lines.caption: Cover a two by six board with dominoes. There are exactly thirteen ways.

lines.text: Next, add an L-shaped tile. How many ways now? Most kids lose count fast.
lines.caption: Next, add an L-shaped tile. How many ways now? Most kids lose count fast.

lines.text: Hello, I'm Vantee. Today we'll count without losing our place!
lines.caption: Hello, I'm Vantee. Today we'll count without losing our place!

lines.text: In how many ways can a two by six board be covered, with no gaps or overlaps,
lines.caption: In how many ways can a two by six board be covered, with no gaps or overlaps,

lines.text: using one by two dominoes, and L-shaped trominoes made of three squares? Pieces may be turned.
lines.caption: using one by two dominoes, and L-shaped trominoes made of three squares? Pieces may be turned.

lines.text: Here are the five choices: thirteen, fifty, fifty-three, fifty-nine, and one hundred seventeen.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices: thirteen, fifty, fifty-three, fifty-nine, and one hundred seventeen.

lines.text: A board two squares tall, six long. That's twelve squares.
lines.caption: A board two squares tall, six long. That's twelve squares.

lines.text: A domino covers two squares. An L tromino covers three, and it can be turned four ways.
lines.caption: A domino covers two squares. An L tromino covers three, and it can be turned four ways.

lines.text: Every square gets covered exactly once. And a cover with only dominoes still counts.
lines.caption: Every square gets covered exactly once. And a cover with only dominoes still counts.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: some tile must cover the top-left square. Which one?
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: some tile must cover the top-left square. Which one?

lines.text: A standing domino leaves a two by five board.
lines.caption: A standing domino leaves a two by five board.

lines.text: A lying domino on top needs a lying twin under it. Nothing else fits. That leaves two by four.
lines.caption: A lying domino on top needs a lying twin under it. Nothing else fits. That leaves two by four.

lines.text: Or an L. Only two L tiles work. This third one would trap the square below it.
lines.caption: Or an L. Only two L tiles work. This third one would trap the square below it.

lines.text: Each good L leaves one square sticking out. A lying domino can fill it, and the bump moves along.
lines.caption: Each good L leaves one square sticking out. A lying domino can fill it, and the bump moves along.

lines.text: Or a second L tile fills it, and closes the block.
lines.caption: Or a second L tile fills it, and closes the block.

lines.text: So an L starts one zigzag: an L, some lying dominoes, then an L. It can be three to six long.
lines.caption: So an L starts one zigzag: an L, some lying dominoes, then an L. It can be three to six long.

lines.text: Each zigzag has a mirror twin, flipped top to bottom. So there are two of every length.
lines.caption: Each zigzag has a mirror twin, flipped top to bottom. So there are two of every length.

lines.text: Let's fill a table, from short to long.
lines.caption: Let's fill a table, from short to long.

lines.text: If a zigzag fills the whole board, that's one way. So length zero counts as one.
lines.caption: If a zigzag fills the whole board, that's one way. So length zero counts as one.

lines.text: Length one: one way. Length two: two standing dominoes, or a lying pair. Two ways.
lines.caption: Length one: one way. Length two: two standing dominoes, or a lying pair. Two ways.

lines.text: The rule: one shorter, plus two shorter, plus double everything the zigzags leave.
lines.caption: The rule: one shorter, plus two shorter, plus double everything the zigzags leave.

lines.text: Length three: two, plus one, plus double one. That's five.
lines.caption: Length three: two, plus one, plus double one. That's five.

lines.text: Now length four: five, plus two, plus double one plus one. That's eleven.
lines.caption: Now length four: five, plus two, plus double one plus one. That's eleven.

lines.text: Length five: eleven, plus five, plus double two plus one plus one. That's twenty-four.
lines.caption: Length five: eleven, plus five, plus double two plus one plus one. That's twenty-four.

lines.text: Length six: twenty-four, plus eleven, plus double five plus two plus one plus one.
lines.caption: Length six: twenty-four, plus eleven, plus double five plus two plus one plus one.

lines.text: That's twenty-four plus eleven plus eighteen: fifty-three ways. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: That's twenty-four plus eleven plus eighteen: fifty-three ways. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Here's a second way: flat boards, and bumpy ones, with one extra square sticking out on the left.
lines.caption: Here's a second way: flat boards, and bumpy ones, with one extra square sticking out on the left.

lines.text: On a flat board, a domino start leaves a flat board. An L leaves a bumpy board, two shorter.
lines.caption: On a flat board, a domino start leaves a flat board. An L leaves a bumpy board, two shorter.

lines.text: There are two good L tiles, so that bumpy count gets doubled.
lines.caption: There are two good L tiles, so that bumpy count gets doubled.

lines.text: On a bumpy board, cover the lonely square first. A lying domino leaves a bumpy board, one shorter.
lines.caption: On a bumpy board, cover the lonely square first. A lying domino leaves a bumpy board, one shorter.

lines.text: An L instead leaves a flat board, one shorter. Add those two.
lines.caption: An L instead leaves a flat board, one shorter. Add those two.

lines.text: Bumpy one is just an L shape: one way. Bumpy two is one plus one, two.
lines.caption: Bumpy one is just an L shape: one way. Bumpy two is one plus one, two.

lines.text: Bumpy three is two plus two, four. Bumpy four is four plus five, nine.
lines.caption: Bumpy three is two plus two, four. Bumpy four is four plus five, nine.

lines.text: Flat six: twenty-four, plus eleven, plus two times nine. Fifty-three again!
lines.caption: Flat six: twenty-four, plus eleven, plus two times nine. Fifty-three again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? For long boards. Just two short rules!
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? For long boards. Just two short rules!

lines.text: Choice A, thirteen, uses dominoes only. It forgets every cover with a tromino.
lines.caption: Choice A, thirteen, uses dominoes only. It forgets every cover with a tromino.

lines.text: Without zigzags, the table goes one, two, three, five, eight, thirteen.
lines.caption: Without zigzags, the table goes one, two, three, five, eight, thirteen.

lines.text: Choice E, one hundred seventeen, is the count for a two by seven board.
lines.caption: Choice E, one hundred seventeen, is the count for a two by seven board.

lines.text: Fifty-three, plus twenty-four, plus double twenty, is one hundred seventeen.
lines.caption: Fifty-three, plus twenty-four, plus double twenty, is one hundred seventeen.

lines.text: Choices B and D, fifty and fifty-nine, are near misses. Both ways give exactly fifty-three.
lines.caption: Choices B and D, fifty and fifty-nine, are near misses. Both ways give exactly fifty-three.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, one new tile.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, one new tile.

lines.text: Cover a two by five board with the same tiles, AND two by two squares. How many ways?
lines.caption: Cover a two by five board with the same tiles, AND two by two squares. How many ways?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. A square on the top-left gives a second way to start, two columns wide.
lines.caption: Let's check. A square on the top-left gives a second way to start, two columns wide.

lines.text: A square can't fill a bump, so the zigzags stay the same.
lines.caption: A square can't fill a bump, so the zigzags stay the same.

lines.text: New rule: one shorter, plus TWO times two shorter, plus double the zigzag leftovers.
lines.caption: New rule: one shorter, plus TWO times two shorter, plus double the zigzag leftovers.

lines.text: Length one: one. Length two: one plus two, three. Length three: three plus two plus two, seven.
lines.caption: Length one: one. Length two: one plus two, three. Length three: three plus two plus two, seven.

lines.text: Now length four: seven, plus double three, plus double one plus one. That's seventeen.
lines.caption: Now length four: seven, plus double three, plus double one plus one. That's seventeen.

lines.text: Length five: seventeen, plus double seven, plus double three plus one plus one. Forty-one!
lines.caption: Length five: seventeen, plus double seven, plus double three plus one plus one. Forty-one!

lines.text: If you got forty-one, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got forty-one, amazing work!

lines.text: To count the ways to tile a strip, ask which tile covers the first square. Then count what's left.
lines.caption: To count the ways to tile a strip, ask which tile covers the first square. Then count what's left.

lines.text: Build up from the short boards, one length at a time.
lines.caption: Build up from the short boards, one length at a time.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
